message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"19.21","text":"And Simon said, “You have said these things correctly. Nevertheless, in the present world does it not seem to you that the human being is receptive to every passion? I mean desire, anger, grief, and such things.” Peter said, “These too belong to things that happen, not to things that always exist; and it will now be found that they happen beneficially to the soul. For desire has come to occur in the living creature from the one who created everything well, so that, led by it toward intercourse, humanity may multiply, from which arises a multitude suitable for the selection of the better ones for eternal life. No one would undertake intercourse with a woman without desire; but now, under the pretext of pleasure, as though gratifying himself, the human being does the Creator’s will. Nevertheless, if someone uses desire for lawful marriage, he is not impious; but if he rushes toward adultery, he acts impiously and is therefore punished, because he has used badly what was established well. Similarly, anger has received from God the nature of being kindled within us, so that it may draw us toward the redress of sins. Nevertheless, someone who uses it without measure acts unjustly, but one who uses it in due proportion carries out what is just. We are also receptive to grief, so that we may possess sympathy at the death of relatives, a wife, children, brothers, parents, friends, or any others; for if we lacked the capacity to suffer with others, we would be inhuman. Similarly, all the other things will be found to be suitably constituted, if indeed the purpose for which each came into being is understood.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν συμβαινόντων","chosen":"things that happen","rationale":"The participle denotes contingent occurrences, contrasted explicitly with things that always exist; “contingent things” is a viable but more technical alternative."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς κοινωνίαν","chosen":"toward intercourse","rationale":"In the context of desire, reproduction, women, marriage, and adultery, κοινωνία denotes sexual union rather than fellowship generally."},{"source_quote":"πλῆθος ἐκλογῆς κρειττόνων γίνεται πρὸς αἰώνιον ζωὴν ἐπιτήδειον","chosen":"arises a multitude suitable for the selection of the better ones for eternal life","rationale":"ἐπιτήδειον most naturally modifies πλῆθος, while ἐκλογῆς κρειττόνων expresses the selection of better ones; the compact Greek permits alternative attachment."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἐκείνου βούλημα","chosen":"the Creator’s will","rationale":"ἐκείνου refers contextually to the one who created everything well, although a more formally ambiguous rendering would be “that one’s will.”"},{"source_quote":"πρὸς ἄμυναν ἁμαρτημάτων","chosen":"toward the redress of sins","rationale":"ἄμυνα may denote defense, resistance, redress, or requital. “Redress” preserves anger’s corrective function without specifying whether the sins are resisted or punished."},{"source_quote":"κατ’ ἀξίαν δὲ χρώμενος","chosen":"one who uses it in due proportion","rationale":"The phrase contrasts measured, fitting use of anger with ἀμέτρῳ, its measureless use; “as deserved” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶν·συμβαινόντων","issue":"A centered dot is printed between the article and participle. The syntax requires them to be construed together, and the translation treats the mark as editorial punctuation without semantic force.","proposed_reading":"τῶν συμβαινόντων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀδελ-. φῶν","issue":"The word is interrupted by a printed line-break hyphen followed by a period and spacing. Its surviving parts transparently yield ἀδελφῶν, translated as “brothers.”","proposed_reading":"ἀδελφῶν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19.22","text":"And Simon said, “Why do people also die before their time, and why do recurring diseases occur, and moreover why do demons, madnesses, and all kinds of sufferings capable of tormenting severely exist?” Peter said, “Because people, yielding everything of theirs to pleasure, have intercourse without observing the proper times, and thus the depositing of their seeds, undertaken at the wrong time, naturally sprouts countless evils. They ought to have reasoned that, just as an appropriate time has been appointed for planting and sowing, so also observable days have been correspondingly assigned for intercourse. Hence someone who had learned from the tradition of Moses, when reproaching the people for sins, called them ‘sons of the new moons according to the moon and of Sabbaths.’ At the beginning of the world people were both long-lived and free from disease; but when they became negligent and abandoned the observance, from that time onward successive sons, because of ignorance, ..... having intercourse when they should not, subject their own children to countless sufferings. Therefore also our .....alos, concerning the person disabled from birth who regained sight through him, when exeta..............en, ‘This man or his parents—he was born blind?’ answered, ‘Neither did this man sin in any way nor did his parents, but it was so that through him the power of God might be manifested,’ healing the sins of ignorance. And truly, such things happen because of ignorance—that is, because a man does not know when he ought to have intercourse with his wife and whether she happens to be clean after menstruation. Nevertheless, the sufferings you previously mentioned arise from ignorance, but they were not produced by an evil one. Furthermore, grant me the person who does not sin, and accept the person who does not suffer, and you may find him able to heal others too so that they do not suffer. For example, Moses, because of his piety, remained free from suffering throughout the whole span of his life, and by his prayers he healed the Egyptians who were suffering because of sin.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀπαρατηρήτως κοινωνοῦσι","chosen":"have intercourse without observing the proper times","rationale":"The following discussion explicitly concerns appointed days for sexual intercourse, so ἀπαρατηρήτως refers to failure to observe those times."},{"source_quote":"ἡ τῶν σπερμάτων καταβολὴ","chosen":"the depositing of their seeds","rationale":"In this reproductive context the phrase refers to the depositing of semen, while retaining the author’s agricultural image of seed."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιτηρήσιμοι ἡμέραι προσῳκείωνται","chosen":"observable days have been correspondingly assigned","rationale":"ἐπιτηρήσιμοι identifies days to be watched or observed, and προσῳκείωνται presents them as appropriately or correspondingly designated."},{"source_quote":"υἱοὺς νεομηνιῶν τῶν κατὰ σελήνην καὶ σαββάτων","chosen":"sons of the new moons according to the moon and of Sabbaths","rationale":"The unusual formulation is preserved rather than replaced with wording from a familiar scriptural passage."},{"source_quote":"εἰ καθαρὰ ἐξ ἀφέδρου τυγχάνει","chosen":"whether she happens to be clean after menstruation","rationale":"In the context of marital intercourse and ritual timing, ἄφεδρος refers to menstrual discharge; “clean from her discharge” is a more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ πονηροῦ","chosen":"by an evil one","rationale":"The substantival adjective can mean an evil being or evil agency. The personal rendering suits the surrounding debate, while “by evil” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"δὸς τὸν μὴ ἁμαρτάνοντα καὶ λαβὲ τὸν μὴ πάσχοντα","chosen":"grant me the person who does not sin, and accept the person who does not suffer","rationale":"The paired imperatives set up the claim that freedom from sin corresponds to freedom from suffering. “Show me … and take it that …” is another possible idiomatic rendering."},{"source_quote":"ἀπαθὴς","chosen":"free from suffering","rationale":"The immediate context concerns disease and other afflictions, favoring freedom from suffering over the philosophical sense “free from passions.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"αἰτίᾳ ..... μὴ δεῖν κοινωνοῦντες","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna. Its unavailable content has not been restored, and all five dots remain in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅθεν καὶ ..... αλος ἡμῶν","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna before the surviving word ending αλος. The ending is retained as “alos”; completing the word, even though the context suggests a title or designation, would require an unsupported restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἔξετα .............. εν οὗτος","issue":"The selected edition prints a fourteen-dot lacuna between the surviving fragments ἔξετα and εν. The translation preserves the fragments by transliteration and supplies no missing question or verb form.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19.23","text":"And Simon said, “Let these things be so. Does not the inequality among human beings seem to you utterly unjust? One person is poor, another is rich; one is sick, and ..... is healthy—and nevertheless there are countless such things in human life.” Peter said, “Do you not perceive, Simon, that once again you are sending your arguments outside the target? For while we are discussing an evil one, you have made a digression and introduced a discussion about seeming irregularities. Nevertheless, I will speak to this as well. The world is an instrument skillfully made so that the female may bear eternal righteous sons for the male who is to exist eternally. But devout people could not be brought to completion here if there were no needy people for them to help. Similarly, for this reason there are also sick people for them to care for, and what follows contains the same reasoning.” Simon said, “Then the lowly have been unfortunate, for they themselves suffer hardship for the making of righteous people.” Peter said, “If their lowliness were eternal, it would be the greatest misfortune. But humiliations and exaltations come to human beings by lot. If the lot does not please someone, it is possible for him to use an appeal, plead his case lawfully, and by that means change his life himself.” Simon said, “What are this lot and appeal?” Peter said, “This is an explanation belonging to another discourse. Nevertheless, if you permit it, we can show you how, after being born anew, changing your birth, and living lawfully, you may obtain eternal salvation.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἀνωμαλία","chosen":"the inequality among human beings","rationale":"ἀνωμαλία can denote unevenness, irregularity, or inequality; the examples contrast poverty with wealth and sickness with health."},{"source_quote":"περὶ πονηροῦ","chosen":"about an evil one","rationale":"The substantival adjective may refer personally to an evil being or abstractly to evil. The personal rendering fits the debate’s preceding distinction between sufferings and an evil agent."},{"source_quote":"τῶν δοκούντων ἀτοπημάτων","chosen":"seeming irregularities","rationale":"The phrase denotes apparent anomalies or absurdities in human circumstances; “apparent injustices” would interpret their moral character more explicitly."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ἐσομένῳ ἄρρενι αἰωνίως ἡ θήλεια τίκτῃ","chosen":"the female may bear … for the male who is to exist eternally","rationale":"The grammatical gender imagery is preserved. The terms may symbolize present and future cosmic orders rather than literal individual sexes, but the passage does not make that referent explicit."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ ἀποτελεσθῆναι δικαίους αὐτοὶ κακουχοῦνται","chosen":"they themselves suffer hardship for the making of righteous people","rationale":"The construction may imply that others become righteous by aiding the lowly, or that the sufferers themselves are perfected as righteous. The contextual complaint favors the former without naming a specific agent."},{"source_quote":"ὁ κλῆρος","chosen":"the lot","rationale":"κλῆρος can mean an allotted portion, fate, or inheritance. “Lot” preserves the subsequent legal metaphor and avoids deciding whether astrological destiny is intended."},{"source_quote":"ἐκκλήτῳ χρησάμενον καὶ νομίμως διαδικασάμενον","chosen":"use an appeal, plead his case lawfully","rationale":"ἔκκλητος and διαδικασάμενον employ juridical language: an appeal followed by lawful litigation or adjudication."},{"source_quote":"τὴν γένεσιν ὑπαλλάξας","chosen":"changing your birth","rationale":"γένεσις can denote birth, origin, or the condition and destiny attached to birth. “Changing your natal condition” is a possible more interpretive alternative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὃς μὲν νοσεῖ καὶ ..... ὑγιαίνει","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna between “one is sick” and “is healthy.” The missing contrasting expression has not been supplied, and the five dots remain explicit.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19.24","text":"And when Simon heard these things, he said, “Do not suppose that, because I kept agreeing while investigating each topic, I proceeded to another topic as though fully persuaded. Rather, I offered you al.....noias of my being persuaded, so that you might move on to another topic, in order that, after learning all your .........noias, I might condemn you without relying on conjecture. But having been fully persuad............ Now allow me three days, and when I return I will show that you know nothing.” When Simon had said this and was about to leave, my father said, “Listen briefly to me, Simon, and then go as you please. I remember how, at the outset before the debate, when you had not yet had experience of me, you leveled prejudgments against me. And now, after repeatedly hearing the debate, recognizing Peter’s superiority, and now granting that he speaks the truth, what do I seem to you—someone who knows how to judge correctly, or not? For if you say that I appear to have judged correctly but you do not agree, you appear prejudiced, being unwilling to concede defeat even after an admission. But if I was not rightly declaring Peter superior in the debate, persuade us how we judged incorrectly—or else do not stop debating him on every point, since it will be yours, as you are defeated and concede each time—or, if you possess this sense of shame, are condemned by all the listeners in place of the greatest punishment and act disgracefully—to have your own soul ache under conscience. For we saw in deed that you have been defeated, but we heard the argument you promise. Ultimately, I do not think that you will come to the debate as you promised; rather, as you were leaving, you promised to return so that you might seem not to be ashamed.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ἕκαστον κεφάλαιον ζητῶν συνετιθέμην","chosen":"I kept agreeing while investigating each topic","rationale":"ζητεῖν here denotes inquiry or debate, while συνετίθετο expresses agreement or concession rather than merely arranging something."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πληροφορούμενος","chosen":"as though fully persuaded","rationale":"The participle denotes being fully assured or convinced; Simon distinguishes outward agreement from genuine conviction."},{"source_quote":"μὴ στοχαζόμενος καταγινώσκω σου","chosen":"I might condemn you without relying on conjecture","rationale":"στοχάζομαι denotes guessing or reaching a conclusion by conjecture, contrasted with learning Simon’s opponent’s complete position."},{"source_quote":"προλήψεις μου κατέφερες","chosen":"you leveled prejudgments against me","rationale":"πρόληψις is a prior assumption or prejudice, and καταφέρω presents Simon as bringing or pronouncing such judgments against the speaker."},{"source_quote":"Πέτρον ἐν ὑπεροχῇ γνοὺς","chosen":"recognizing Peter’s superiority","rationale":"ἐν ὑπεροχῇ indicates Peter’s superior position or performance in the debate."},{"source_quote":"ἔκαστοτε ἠττωμένῳ καὶ συντιθεμένῳ","chosen":"as you are defeated and concede each time","rationale":"In a disputational context συντίθεμαι means to agree or concede after being overcome in argument."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ συνειδήσεως τὴν σεαυτοῦ ἀλγεῖν ψυχήν","chosen":"to have your own soul ache under conscience","rationale":"The wording preserves the image of Simon’s own soul being pained under the pressure of conscience."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ δοκεῖν μὴ αἰδεῖσθαι","chosen":"so that you might seem not to be ashamed","rationale":"The phrase concerns the appearance Simon intends to create by promising to return; “so as not to appear ashamed” is an idiomatic alternative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀλ.....νοίας σοι τοῦ πείθεσθαι παρεῖχον","issue":"A five-dot lacuna interrupts an otherwise unidentified word or phrase between the surviving fragments αλ and νοίας. The translation retains those fragments as “al.....noias” and does not infer the missing noun.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πάσας ......... νοίας σου","issue":"The selected edition prints a nine-dot lacuna before the surviving ending νοίας. The unavailable wording has not been restored; the ending is retained by transliteration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀλλὰ πεπληροφορημε ............","issue":"The selected edition prints a twelve-dot lacuna after the incomplete form πεπληροφορημε. The translation gives the discernible sense of the surviving stem as a broken English form and retains all twelve dots without completing the sentence.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"μετὰ ὁμολογίαν . ἦτταν συνθέσθαι μὴ θέλων","issue":"The printed full stop produces an abrupt syntactic division between ὁμολογίαν and ἦτταν. The translation construes the wording as a continuous thought about admitting and conceding defeat while preserving the selected edition rather than treating the punctuation as an OCR error.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19.25","text":"When Simon heard this, he ground his teeth in anger and went away in silence. Since a considerable part of the day still remained, Peter laid his hands on the large crowd for healing, dismissed them, entered the house with his closer companions, and sat down. Then one of the followers, named Sophonias, said, “Blessed is God, Peter, who chose you and filled you with wisdom for the sake of right-minded people. For truly, you debated Simon with great force and patience. We also ask you to discourse to us about evil things, hoping that you will set forth for us more genuinely the discourse concerning it—and not at this very hour, but tomorrow, if it pleases you. For we make allowance for you because of the fatigue from the debate.” Peter said, “I want you to know that the person who does something with pleasure is refreshed by the very labors involved, but the person who does not do what he desires is wearied most greatly by rest itself. Thus, by making me discuss the things dear to me, you grant me the great benefits of rest.” Nevertheless, content with his willingness and sharing his labors into the night—as it was his custom with those who were genui..... to converse—we asked that the postponement be made. And then, after partaking of salt, we ........pēmen to sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"χειροθετήσας πρὸς ἴασιν","chosen":"laid his hands … for healing","rationale":"The stated purpose is healing, so χειροθετέω describes the laying on of hands rather than appointment to an office."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τῶν συνηθεστέρων","chosen":"with his closer companions","rationale":"The comparative adjective denotes those more accustomed or intimate with Peter, not merely the entire group of followers."},{"source_quote":"τῶν εὐγνωμόνων","chosen":"right-minded people","rationale":"εὐγνώμων can mean discerning, well-disposed, reasonable, or grateful. “Right-minded” fits those able to receive Peter’s wisdom."},{"source_quote":"μεγάλως καὶ ἀνεξικάκως","chosen":"with great force and patience","rationale":"μεγάλως marks the impressive strength of the debate, while ἀνεξικάκως denotes patient endurance of hostility or injury."},{"source_quote":"περὶ πονηρῶν","chosen":"about evil things","rationale":"The plural substantival adjective can denote evil things, evil matters, or evil beings. The following singular αὐτοῦ refers back to the subject collectively, so the less specific “evil things” is retained."},{"source_quote":"γνησιώτερόν σε ἡμῖν τὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ ἐκφᾶναι λόγον","chosen":"set forth for us more genuinely the discourse concerning it","rationale":"γνησιώτερον may mean more genuinely, candidly, or intimately, reflecting the contrast between instruction to close followers and public debate."},{"source_quote":"ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν καμάτων ἀναπαύεται","chosen":"is refreshed by the very labors involved","rationale":"The paradox is preserved: pleasurable work itself provides the person’s rest or refreshment."},{"source_quote":"ἁλῶν μεταλαβόντες","chosen":"after partaking of salt","rationale":"The phrase literally refers to sharing or consuming salt and may idiomatically imply eating a meal; the source’s concrete image is retained."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς τοὺς γνησι..... λέγεσθαι","issue":"A five-dot lacuna divides the surviving beginning γνησι from the surviving verbal material λέγεσθαι. The translation renders the discernible fragments around the gap but does not restore a designation for the people or a compound verb.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἰς ὕπνον........πημεν","issue":"The selected edition prints an eight-dot lacuna before the surviving ending πημεν. Because that ending does not independently identify the lost verb, it is retained as “pēmen” rather than expanded into a conjectural verb of going or turning.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
